clue.text: County players feeling despondent

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
the cast is the group of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A county cricket team is gloomy after a bad result.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone downcast is dejected and low in spirits, a synonym for despondent.

clue.text: Top English horror film

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen
horror is extreme fear or dread

explanation.surface: A leading English horror movie is being praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horror film' reads as one phrase, but 'horror' gives FEAR and 'film' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Fear is a 1962 thriller, remade by Martin Scorsese in 1991, so it is an example of a movie.

clue.text: Up against it, adult inside points out

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the other's letters
out signals that the letters of points are put out of order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film certificates

explanation.surface: A grown-up, being in trouble, picks out the flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes INSPOT, and 'inside' places the adult's letter within it; 'points out' looks like one verb phrase meaning to indicate.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up against it is to face serious difficulty, the same idiom as being in trouble or a tight corner.

clue.text: Act as witness at critical trial

parts.note: a test is a decisive trial or examination

explanation.surface: Someone gives evidence at a crucial court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true, as a witness does in court.

clue.text: Us soldier getting married, allowed a cocktail

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
M is the abbreviation for married in genealogies and forms
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: An American serviceman, having wed, is permitted a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimlet is a mixed drink of gin and lime juice, an example of a cocktail.

clue.text: Be ruthless, thanks to vast sums reflecting no object

indicators.note: reflecting, like a mirror image, signals that the joined words thanks and vast sums are read backwards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
pots of money are large sums
no object is nothing at all

explanation.surface: Someone says money is no object when asked how ruthless to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' turns TA + POTS, giving STOPAT; 'no object' supplies NOTHING. 'Ta' is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop at nothing is an idiom for being willing to do anything, however ruthless, to get what one wants.

clue.text: Easily made angry, the rep stormed off

indicators.note: off suggests the words have gone wrong or gone off, so the letters of the rep stormed are rearranged

explanation.surface: The sales representative lost their temper easily and stormed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormed' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'off' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-tempered person flares up quickly, the same as being irritable or quick to anger.

clue.text: Antiseptic man applied to boy and girl

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
Ian is a boy's name
Violet is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man is put together with a boy and a girl, as if making a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentian violet is a purple dye once widely painted on wounds and skin infections as a disinfectant.

clue.text: Throw out black cat

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get rid of an unlucky black cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce, or snow leopard, is a crossword favourite for 'cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce someone is to eject them, as a nightclub doorman does with troublemakers.

clue.text: Lump — provide information about source

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
a well is a source of water, or figuratively of anything

explanation.surface: Someone asks for details about where a lump came from.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'sing' is criminal slang for informing on accomplices.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling is a raised bump on the body, the same as a lump.

clue.text: Dandy and beano finally brought in by former pupil

indicators.note: brought in by means taken inside the other piece

parts.note: FP is the abbreviation for former pupil, used in school alumni lists

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of beano

explanation.surface: Two comics, the Dandy and the Beano, are brought in by an old boy of the school.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy and the Beano are long-running British children's comics, which makes 'Dandy' look like a title; it is the definition. A 'beano' is also a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a man overly concerned with his clothes and appearance, a synonym for a dandy.

clue.text: A guy in a comfortably relaxed frame of mind

definitions.text: in a comfortably relaxed frame of mind

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or rib them, to tease

explanation.surface: A man is described as being calm and relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a noun, a man, but here it is the verb meaning to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at ease means feeling calm and untroubled, a relaxed state of mind.

clue.text: Get ahead of foreign tourist before parking

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the parking letter
foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters of tourist are rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An overseas visitor hurries to get ahead of others before finding a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to outrun or overtake, leaving a rival behind.

clue.text: Therefore pawn gets a bribe

parts.note: so means therefore
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker accepts a bribe as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pawn' suggests pawnbroking, but it is the chess piece, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a small concession or payment given to placate someone, a kind of bribe.

clue.text: Partners back film

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A couple go to see a movie together.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge West and East (W, E) play as partners against North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a cowboy movie, a genre of film.

clue.text: Stray inside border region

indicators.note: inside shows the letters are found within the words border region

explanation.surface: Someone wanders into a frontier area.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to wander from the right path or make a mistake, the same as to stray.

clue.text: Bird got in annexe after friend returned

indicators.note: after places the annexe piece following the reversed friend
returned means sent back, so the word for friend is read in reverse

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a wing is an extension or annexe of a building

explanation.surface: A bird got into an extension after a friend came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PAL into LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, or peewit, is a crested plover, a species of bird.

clue.text: Covering the whole distance, continually

definitions.meaning: the whole length of something, from end to end
the whole time, from the start

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means along the entire length of something, and also throughout or all the time, as in knowing something from the beginning.

clue.text: Battle later resolved in court

indicators.note: in places the rearranged word inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: resolved suggests something worked out anew, so the letters of later are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fight was later settled in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' makes ATERL from LATER, placed 'in' WOO. 'court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb, to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo was the 1815 battle in which Napoleon was finally defeated.

clue.text: Takes part in a race, and finishes

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
ends means finishes

explanation.surface: A competitor enters a race and completes it.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it and participate, to take part in it.

clue.text: Blow up and erupt, possibly enveloping country's capital

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the rearranged letters go around the capital letter
possibly hints at a different arrangement of the letters of erupt
capital means the first, or head, letter of country's

explanation.surface: A volcano blows up and erupts, perhaps engulfing a nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes PERUT from ERUPT, and 'enveloping' wraps it round C; 'Blow up' looks like one phrase, but 'Blow' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a boxing punch thrown upward at the chin, a type of blow.

clue.text: Stoat in mere, swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about, so in mere is rearranged

explanation.surface: A stoat is swimming in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it is part of the fodder. A mere is a small lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the stoat, especially in its white winter coat, so the two name the same animal.

clue.text: Composer's church work, popular

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A composer's work for church is well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Composer' is a link, short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic who wrote mainly for piano, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: The French on excursion act without restraint

parts.note: le is French for the
a trip is an outing or excursion

explanation.surface: French people on an outing behave wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for acting or speaking freely and unrestrainedly.

clue.text: Duck left out for a meal

indicators.note: out means left out, so the letter for left is removed

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck

explanation.surface: Duck is left off the menu for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon meal, or in parts of Britain the evening meal.

clue.text: Flower border — talk tediously about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the talking word goes around the border word

parts.note: to prose is to speak or write at dull length
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A gardener drones on about a flower border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring wildflower.

clue.text: Noble, frightfully droll by end of party

indicators.note: frightfully suggests something terribly mixed up, so the letters of droll are rearranged
end of picks out the last letter of party

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is terribly amusing at the end of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightfully' looks like an intensifier for 'droll', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly means befitting a lord, grand or aristocratic, much as noble does.

clue.text: Dog — daughter and I mind one barking at end of street

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of mind one are scrambled
at end of picks out the last letter of street

explanation.surface: A dog barks at the end of the street, bothering a father and daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' makes EDINMON from MIND ONE. 'Barking' (mad) is British slang, and it looks like the dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dandie Dinmont is a long-bodied Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.
